subject: Evidence request: deploy policy exceptions and temporary credential usage
messages:
From: Audits Team <audits@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: sig-assessor@security-partners.io
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: change exceptions & temporary credential usage (SOC 2)

Hi Jordan,

We're working through the scoped SOC2 items and need artifacts related to deploy policy exceptions and temporary credential issuance for the last 12 months. Specifically, could you provide: 

- A register of approved deploy-policy exceptions (who approved, justification, expiration)
- Audit/log of temporary credential issuances (just-in-time keys, short-lived API tokens)
- Keystore rotation history showing dates and responsible approvers
- A snapshot of PR approvals/Code Review traces for commits that required exceptions

If possible, please include any evidence that maps exceptions to compensating controls (e.g., monitoring, timeboxed access). We may follow up with a few targeted questions after review.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Auditor, FinServCo
audits@finservco.com

---
This request is in scope for our Q4 assessor window (SIG/SOC2).
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Audits Team <audits@finservco.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: change exceptions & temporary credential usage (SOC 2)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the initial artifacts that cover the last 12 months:

- keystore-rotation-log.csv (rotations, operator, approver, PR refs)
- temp-creds-issuance-log.csv (issued token IDs, requester, TTL, reason)
- deploy-exception-register.xlsx (exception id, approver, duration, compensating controls)
- pr-approval-snapshot.pdf (filtered PR list + approver usernames)

High-level notes: 
- Deploy exceptions are tracked in the exception register; each entry is paired with a monitoring rule (alerts) and a timebound expiration by default (14 days unless extended).
- Temporary credentials are issued via the internal shortlived-cred service; issuance requires a owner-approved Jira ticket and an automated TTL of 4 hours by default.
- Keystore rotations are performed with KMS-backed workflows; the CSV includes the rotation commit SHAs and the PR numbers.

Links: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4321
Evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLCEvidence

If you need additional context mapping to a specific incident or ticket, flag which IDs and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Audits Team <audits@finservco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: change exceptions & temporary credential usage (SOC 2)

Quick additions from engineering: 
- Included in the keystore CSV are the commit SHAs for the rotation orchestration (column: rotation_commit). We also exported a small CodeOwners screenshot showing which teams have write access for the rotation playbook.
- For PR traceability, note that all exception-related PRs require two code reviewers + one security approver; the PR PDF includes reviewer usernames and timestamps.
- If the assessor wants cryptographic proof of the HSM interactions, we can extract a limited audit stream (redacted) — let us know the timeframe.

--
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Audits Team <audits@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: sig-assessor@security-partners.io
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: change exceptions & temporary credential usage (SOC 2)

Thanks Jordan and Irene — this is a helpful package. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Can you map any deploy exceptions to incident FIN-2025-07 (we have a flagged incident to reconcile)? We need to see whether an exception was open at that time and what compensating monitoring existed.
2) Who is your KMS/HSM provider and can you share the provider attestation or certificate? We need confirmation that a dedicated HSM-backed KMS was used for keystore rotations.

If you can provide those two pieces (timeline mapping + KMS attestation) we'll move to the next review phase.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Senior Auditor, FinServCo
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Audits Team <audits@finservco.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: change exceptions & temporary credential usage (SOC 2)

Maya — attached is the KMS provider certificate and a quick mapping table in the drive folder that ties deploy-exception IDs to incident FIN-2025-07. Summary below: 

- KMS provider: AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys (customer-managed CMKs). Attached: kms-provider-cert.pdf (public attestation provided by vendor).
- Mapping: Exception EX-247 was active during the FIN-2025-07 window (2025-07-12 to 2025-07-20). Compensating controls in place: enhanced logging to Splunk (saved search: KEystoreAudit), 1:1 live monitoring on rotation jobs, and a timebound rollback runbook.

If you want a redacted HSM audit stream for the exact rotation run, we can generate one — this will take 48 hours to sanitize. Let us know if you want that output.

Attachments: kms-provider-cert.pdf
Drive mapping: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLCEvidence (file: EX-247_mapping_sheet.xlsx)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
